newsitem.title: TURKEY: Quakes shake Turkey, five hurt, homes damaged.
newsitem.headline: Quakes shake Turkey, five hurt, homes damaged.

text.p: Two earthquakes measuring 3.8 and 5.5 on the open-ended Richter scale shook southern Turkey on Wednesday evening, injuring five people and damaging a number of houses, Antolian news agency said.

It said five people were injured when 10 houses collapsed in Antakya town, at the eastern end of the Mediterranean near the Syrian border, after the stronger quake hit the town at 7.57 p.m. (1757 GMT).
Anatolian said power and telephone lines were cut off in the city, which officials said was the epicentre of the earthquake, and many residents had left their homes in fear of aftershocks.
An earthquake shook Beirut at about the same time and a Lebanese seismologist said it measured 5.7 on the Richter scale.
Resident also reported the ground shaking in the northern Lebanese city of Tripoli and Nicosia in Cyprus. There were no immediate reports of damage or casualties in Lebanon and Cyprus.
In Turkey the quakes were felt in cities as far away as Izmir in the west and Diyarbakir in the southeast and the southern towns of Mersin and Adana.
Nearly 40 houses were damaged in Denizli province in central-western Turkey, Anatolian said.
Officials from Kandilli Observatory in Istanbul said earlier the epicentre of one of the quakes was in the Aegean Sea and that of the other in the Mediterranean Sea.

In Lebanon, Seismologist Charles Thabet said: "The earthquake which measured 5.7 on the Richter scale had its epicentre 323 km (200 miles) northwest of the observatory of Bhannes -- 25 km (15 miles) north of Beirut."
"It was in the direction of Cyprus and was followed by two or three aftershocks with lower magnitude," he added.
Earthquakes measuring around five on the Richter scale are powerful enough to cause heavy damage in a populated area.
